purpose: Summative evidence for B1.6 (fair-share with 2-10 sharers) and B1.7 (1/3 = 2/6 equivalence).
student_learning_goal: I can share a small collection fairly between 2, 3, 4, or 6 friends, and tell that one third equals two sixths.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can share a small collection fairly between 2, 3, 4, or 6 friends, and tell that one third equals two sixths.
header.character_watermark: Hugo, Tina, and Ona together in the top-right corner. Small (~1.5in tall combined).

parts.student_instructions: Share each collection of cookies fairly. Draw the share onto each plate. Write how many cookies on each plate.
parts.visual_layout: Top of the page. Two share scenes stacked. Scene A: 8 cookies for 4 friends. Scene B: 12 cookies for 6 friends.

image_placeholders.description: Two share scenes stacked in B&W line-art. Each scene ~7in × 2.2in. Scene A: a tray with 8 cookies on the left, 4 paper plates on the right. Scene B: a tray with 12 cookies on the left, 6 paper plates on the right. Each plate ~1.2in diameter.
image_placeholders.placement: Top of the page; two scenes stacked.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P1_TWO_EVEN_SHARES: keywords (cookies, plates, share) name what the scenes show.

parts.answer_key: Scene A: 2 cookies on each plate. Scene B: 2 cookies on each plate.

parts.student_instructions: Share each collection fairly. Cut the leftover into the right fraction. Write the per-plate share.
parts.visual_layout: Middle of the page. Two share scenes stacked. Scene A: 7 cookies for 3 friends (each = 2 1/3). Scene B: 9 cookies for 6 friends (each = 1 1/2).

image_placeholders.description: Two share scenes stacked in B&W line-art. Each scene ~7in × 2.2in. Scene A: 7 cookies (6 whole + 1 with pre-drawn third-lines) on the left, 3 paper plates on the right. Scene B: 9 cookies (6 whole + 3 with pre-drawn sixth-lines, OR 6 whole + 3 with pre-drawn half-lines) on the left, 6 paper plates on the right. Pre-drawn fraction-lines are dotted lines on the leftover cookies.
image_placeholders.placement: Middle of the page; two scenes stacked.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P2_TWO_FRACTIONAL: keywords (cookies, plates, fraction) name what the scenes show.

parts.answer_key: Scene A: 2 1/3 on each plate (2 whole + 1/3). Scene B: 1 1/2 on each plate (1 whole + 1/2). Note: 9÷6 = 1 with 3 leftover; cut each of the 3 leftovers in half = 6 halves; one half per plate = 1 1/2 each.

parts.part_title: Part 3: One Third Equals Two Sixths
parts.student_instructions: Two pizzas. Shade 1/3 of the first pizza. Shade 2/6 of the second pizza. Then write the equation: 1/3 = ___/___.
parts.visual_layout: Lower-middle of the page. Two pizzas side by side. Pizza A: divided into 3 thirds. Pizza B: divided into 6 sixths.

image_placeholders.description: Two circular pizzas in B&W line-art, side by side, each ~3in diameter. Pizza A has two crossed lines from a single intersection forming 3 equal sectors. Pizza B has 3 lines from the centre forming 6 equal sectors. Each pizza has a thin black border. Below the pizzas, an equation line '1/3 = ___/___'.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P3_TWO_PIZZAS: keywords (pizza, thirds, sixths) name what the pizzas show.

parts.answer_key: Pizza A: one of the 3 sectors shaded. Pizza B: two of the 6 sectors shaded. Equation: 1/3 = 2/6.

parts.student_instructions: Why does 1/3 equal 2/6? Write 1-2 sentences to explain.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. A blank lined area (~7in × 1.5in) for the child to write. A small thinking-bubble icon in the top-right corner.

image_placeholders.description: A blank lined writing area in B&W line-art, ~7in × 1.5in, with 3-4 dotted writing lines. A small thinking-bubble icon (~0.8in tall) in the top-right corner.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P4_WHY_EQUAL_BOX: keywords (explain, equal) name what the box asks for.

parts.answer_key: Open. Accept any plausible reasoning that touches on (a) the same total amount of pizza is shaded and (b) more sharers means smaller pieces but more of them. Examples: '1/3 and 2/6 cover the same amount of pizza. The pizza is just cut differently.' 'When you cut a third in half, you get 2 sixths.'

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, draw your own equivalence: shade 2/3 of one pizza and the same amount of a second pizza divided into sixths. What is 2/3 equal to in sixths?
teacher_notes: Lesson 5 capstone summative worksheet. Hand out at the end of the Action phase. Use Parts 1-4 as the summative evidence for B1.6 + B1.7. Watch for: (a) Part 2 Scene A children who cut the leftover in half instead of in thirds — flag for the match-fraction-to-sharers reteach; (b) Part 3 children who don't shade exactly 2 of the 6 sectors — flag for the overlay-demo reteach; (c) Part 4 children who can't articulate WHY 1/3 = 2/6 — this is the deepest understanding marker; flag for additional pizza-overlay practice.
